doc.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013

title: Extended family and the Holocaust
summary: What became of his father's relatives; some escaped to Palestine, others died in the Holocaust.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. And I wonder, did some of your extended family, aunts, uncles, etcetera, not take advantage of the opportunity to get out at that time?

Most of my father’s — his sister, his youngest brother was killed in World War I, he was a soldier. He was an Austrian soldier and he was killed by the Russians on the Russian front. He had another brother and two sisters. And his mother, of course, after my grandfather had died, was still there. When the war broke out, World War I that is, my father went and got them all out of there because it was very near the Russian border, and they were afraid of the Russians. Because the Russians were noted for pogroms against Jews. Not all of them, but the Cossacks — and so it was a dangerous situation. So he went back and got them, brought them all, they all settled in Vienna. So they were initially, they were not captured when World War II broke out, but, but, unfortunately some got away to Czechoslovakia, some of my relatives, and eventually made their way to what was then Palestine. But my father’s one sister and one brother and his mother were all victims of the holocaust.
